headline: High-risk shared-write and workflow-conflict pair: ECC can modify local state and Superset can ingest outputs, creating default-path data leakage and cascading error risks.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: ECC can write files, use MCP, and run browsers; Superset exposes an API and can consume external inputs. A shared workspace or copied outputs could let attacker-controlled content from one agent influence the other, but no direct shared channel is documented. Because the interaction is inferred from documented surfaces, not proven, I choose medium.
conditions: IF ECC and Superset share a filesystem, clipboard, or MCP bridge
IF Superset ingests content produced by ECC without provenance checks
mitigations: Separate working directories for each agent
Disable clipboard-based handoff between agents
Require provenance tags on all inter-agent files
Review any MCP bridge configuration
requires-engineering: add content-sanitizing wrappers before handoff

B_data_leakage.rationale: ECC touches session summaries, learned skills, hooks, and git history, while Superset has API access and allowlisted egress. If they share a workspace or credentials, sensitive local artifacts from ECC could flow into Superset outputs or API calls. The profiles do not prove a shared workspace, so this is inferred but plausible enough for medium.
conditions: IF both agents operate on the same workspace or home directory
IF ECC session files or hooks contain secrets and are readable by Superset-connected workflows
mitigations: Store each agent in a separate home directory
Restrict Superset access to non-sensitive datasets
Rotate any shared credentials immediately
Audit files under ~/.claude and ~/.cursor/ecc
requires-engineering: enforce per-agent filesystem ACLs

C_capability_conflict.rationale: ECC can modify git state, write the filesystem, and spawn subprocesses; Superset can also act through its API and network egress. If both are pointed at the same mutable repo or workspace, concurrent writes can clobber state or create inconsistent artifacts. The profiles document overlapping mutation surfaces, so high is warranted.
conditions: IF both agents write to the same repository or directory
IF either agent performs concurrent updates without locking
mitigations: Assign separate repos or branches
Pause one agent during the other's write phase
Use file locks for shared artifacts
Commit frequently to reduce conflict windows
requires-engineering: add orchestrator-level concurrency control

D_cascading_error.rationale: ECC produces session summaries, learned skills, documentation, and security findings; Superset can consume API-driven inputs and present analytics. If Superset treats ECC output as authoritative, an error in ECC can propagate into dashboards or downstream actions. No verification step is documented, so the pathway exists but is not shown to be default-dangerous.
conditions: IF Superset ingests ECC-generated text or findings as trusted input
IF no human or automated verification step is inserted before publication
mitigations: Require review before publishing ECC outputs
Mark ECC outputs as untrusted in Superset
Add schema validation on imported records
Limit ECC output to summaries only
requires-engineering: implement provenance-aware ingestion

E_compliance.rationale: ECC explicitly handles session retention settings and security findings, while Superset's profile shows no sensitive data classes or special compliance claims. A compliance mismatch is possible if ECC stores regulated content and Superset republishes it, but the profiles do not show a concrete residency or certification conflict. One-agent citations are insufficient here because the risk is not clearly pairwise.
conditions: IF regulated data is placed into ECC session artifacts
IF Superset exports or retains that same regulated data beyond policy
mitigations: Avoid placing regulated data in ECC sessions
Set short retention on ECC artifacts
Review Superset export settings
Document data-class handling rules
requires-engineering: align retention and residency policies
